Assessment Task – Writing a Technological Brief
Write a complete Technological Brief for an item of your choice.
Your brief must clearly describe the key requirements that the final outcome must meet.
To achieve this, include all of the following:

✅ 1. Key Purpose / Function
Clearly explain what the outcome must do and why it is needed.

✅ 2. Stakeholder Needs
Identify your stakeholder(s) and describe their needs, wants, and expectations for the outcome.

✅ 3. Performance Specifications
Use correct technological terminology to describe the measurable requirements your solution must meet, such as:

Functional attributes (what it must do)

Aesthetic attributes (appearance/feel)

Technical attributes (materials, strength, durability, safety)

Quality standards

Constraints (time, cost, materials, tools, environment)

✅ 4. Success Criteria
State how you will judge whether the final outcome is successful.

These should be specific, measurable, and linked to your performance specifications.

Your Task:
Write your brief in clear, formal technological language.
Make sure each section is explained in full so another designer could understand exactly what they need to produce.

If you'd like, I can also:
📌 create a marking schedule,
📌 generate an exemplar brief, or
📌 turn this into a student worksheet or Google Doc template.

Re write give some examples of physical products also give a glossary of terms that they could use

Here is an improved, student-friendly version with examples of physical products and a glossary of key technological terms.

Assessment Task – Writing a Technological Brief
Write a complete Technological Brief for a physical product of your choice.
Examples you may choose from include:

A phone stand

A bedside lamp

A storage organiser

A planter box

A pet feeder

A desk tidy

A small piece of furniture (stool, shelf, side table)

A wearable item (key tag, badge, simple accessory)

You may also choose any other physical, manufactured outcome that you can realistically design and make.

Your Brief Must Include the Following Sections
✅ 1. Key Purpose / Function
Explain what your product must do and why it is needed.
Example: “The phone stand must hold a smartphone at a readable angle for hands-free viewing on a desk.”

✅ 2. Stakeholder Needs
Identify at least one stakeholder (the person who needs the product) and describe:

Their needs (must have)

Their wants (nice to have)

Their preferences (style, colours, materials)

✅ 3. Performance Specifications
Use correct terminology to give measurable, detailed requirements your product must meet. Include:

Functional attributes (how it works)

Aesthetic attributes (colour, style, appearance)

Technical attributes (materials, durability, safety, strength, dimensions)

Quality standards (finish, accuracy, stability)

Constraints (time, cost, tools, size limits, materials available)

✅ 4. Success Criteria
Write clear, measurable statements that describe how you will know your outcome is successful.
These must link directly to your performance specifications.

Glossary of Useful Technological Terms
Term	Meaning
Stakeholder	A person who has a real need for the outcome and gives feedback.
Attributes	The qualities or features of the product (functional, aesthetic, technical).
Functional attribute	A requirement about how the product must work.
Aesthetic attribute	A requirement about how the product looks or feels.
Technical attribute	A requirement about materials, construction, safety, strength, or measurements.
Performance specifications	Detailed, measurable statements describing what the product must achieve.
Constraints	Limits you must work within (time, cost, materials, tools).
Quality standards	Expectations for accuracy, finish, durability, and overall workmanship.
Success criteria	Statements used to judge whether the final product meets the brief.
End-user	The person who will use the product.
Aesthetics	The visual style or appearance of the product.
Ergonomics	How comfortable and easy a product is to use.
Durability	How long the product will last under normal use.
Sustainability	How environmentally friendly the materials and processes are.
